children: a $160-billion Load Our Bureau Mumbai: Uday Kotak, founder of Kotak Mahindra Bank, described India's foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR(B)) deposit mobilisation scheme as a "strong insurance policy" against global economic and geopolitical shocks, but warned that policymakers must prepare for repayments of $160 billion to $170 billion, including interest, over the next three to five years.

Kotak, speaking at the Business Standard BFSI Summit, said the government and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had acted at the right time by mobilising foreign currency deposits amid heightened geopolitical tensions following the Middle East conflict and the Russia-Ukraine war.

The scheme has strengthened India's foreign currency resources while the country continued to build its domestic macroeconomic fundamentals, he said. "Some people have called the FCNR(B) as a steroid, but I think about it as a strong insurance policy," Kotak said, arguing that the funds had bought India valuable time to prepare for future external financing pressures.

However, he cautioned that the money would eventually have to be repaid and the total repayment obligation, including interest, could rise to $160 billion-$170 billion. Indian banks have mobilised $133 billion under the FCNR(B) swap window. "We don't need to panic about it today, but we must be strategic about it," Kotak said, urging policymakers and financial sector participants to prepare for the repayment pressure well before the deposits mature.

He said that the RBI decision to close the scheme on August 31 helped India lock in foreign currency funding before US bond yields rose sharply early September. The increase in yields would have made the borrowing at least 100 basis points more expensive had India mobilised the funds later, he said.

title: FCNR(B) Funding an Insurance, but it has to be Paid Back: Uday Kotak
